Devlog

What's changing in Tailwinds, update by update. The game ships improvements most days, and every significant one is written up here for players: 184 updates since June 2026, newest first. For discussion, bug reports, and sneak peeks, join the Discord.

November 2026

19 updates · read the month in full

  • Nov 9The Advisor, and a briefing for your own AIA new Advisor page under Company reads your airline and lists what to do about it, most urgent first: aircraft sitting idle (with a button that opens the Route Finder on that type), aircraft with hours to…
  • Nov 9Belly cargo: freight in the holds of your passenger flights (new games)Games you start from today carry freight under the cabin floor. Games already in progress keep freight on freighters only, and nothing in them changes. You can switch it off on the setup screen.
  • Nov 9Guides and in-game help brought back in line with the gameDelivery times read correctly. The Market screen and the in-game Wiki used to say a turboprop arrives in one week and a widebody in four. The first aircraft of a type has always taken twice that, and newer…
  • Nov 8Replace a whole type in one goRetire a type without tagging aircraft one by one. Open any order in your order queue and use Replace a whole type: every aircraft of that type on order that isn’t already replacing something takes over one of…
  • Nov 6See the cabin: floor plans, cabin painting and seat productsA floor plan of the real aircraft. The cabin refit screen now draws the aircraft from above with every seat on it, so you can see what a layout looks like before you pay for it.
  • Nov 6Tail logos and custom tailsDesign your tail. The logo maker has a new Tail section: five designs, your own tail and design colours, and your logo on the fin if you want it.
  • Nov 6A clearer map, and where the money wentLine width by traffic. Switch on Width on the Network map and busier routes are drawn thicker, by last week’s passengers.

  • Nov 6New games: frequency sells seats, a world economy, and a board that sets goalsGames you start from today run a newer set of rules. Games already in progress keep playing exactly as before.
  • Nov 5Smoother with a big airline: faster pages, quieter in the backgroundThe game sits still when you do. The “next week in…” countdown used to make the whole game redraw itself every second, whatever page you had open. Now only the countdown ticks, so a big Fleet or Finance page…
  • Nov 5Freighter conversionsOld passenger jets now have a second career. If you own an aircraft whose family has a freighter version, open it in Fleet and click Convert to freighter. It goes into the hangar and comes back as that…
  • Nov 5Route Finder presetsIf you hunt for routes the same few ways, you no longer have to set the Route Finder up from scratch each time. Set up a search, click + Save this search and give it a name. It appears as a preset above the…
  • Nov 5Randomized worlds: preview, roll until, and shareRandomized passenger demand used to be a blind draw. You only saw a world after you launched it, and its number was gone once the game began. Now:
  • Nov 5Freight now connects through your airportsUntil now a freighter route only carried freight between its own two cities. Fly Hong Kong–Anchorage and Anchorage–Chicago and you got nothing from Hong Kong–Chicago freight, even though that is exactly how…
  • Nov 5Your Gates remembers how you sort it, on phones tooFrom a Discord request by VodkaOnFire: the gate list kept going back to region order with North America on top. The table view already remembered your sort; the card view you get on a phone didn’t have one.
  • Nov 5Aircraft fly up to 100 hours a week (new games)Each aircraft could be scheduled for 140 block hours a week: 20 hours a day, every day. Real airlines don’t fly their aircraft that hard; a busy A321 or 737 manages 9 to 11 hours a day. In new games the limit…
  • Nov 5Rivals stop to refuel, and chase the routes you gave them (new games)In era games, AI airlines no longer give up on long routes the aircraft of the day can’t fly nonstop.
  • Nov 5Filters for fleet renewalPicking which aircraft a new order replaces got a lot quicker on a big fleet.
  • Nov 4Eight 1960s–70s freighters, and a more efficient A220Era games used to jump from the An-12 (1959) straight to the DC-10-30F (1980), so a 1960s cargo airline had nothing to move up to for twenty years. These fill the gap, in order of entry into service:

  • Jul 28Maintenance gets its own page — and you can build your own hangarsMaintenance used to be a slider buried in Operations and a queue of checks you booked one aircraft at a time. It is now a place you go, with a network you build. Company &rsaquo; Maintenance holds the whole…
  • Jul 27Reserve aircraft — station a spare, and breakdowns stop costing you the weekWhen an aircraft blows an engine or disappears into a D check, its routes have always just sat there earning nothing until it came back. Requested by the community: you can now station an idle aircraft as a…
  • Jul 27Change a route’s frequency without closing itFlying six a week when the load factor says you should be flying seven used to mean closing the route, freeing the aircraft and opening the whole thing again — paying the launch cost a second time and losing…
  • Jul 27Point the Routes page at one airport — and a proper table for freightOnce a network passes forty or fifty routes, the Routes page stops being a list you read and becomes a list you scroll. The question you actually want to ask it is almost always about one airport: what am I…
  • Jul 27The aircraft picker now only offers aircraft you can actually useOpening a route meant scrolling a dropdown that listed your entire passenger fleet — including aircraft that the game was always going to refuse. An aircraft can only pick up an extra route that touches an…
  • Jul 27Hub congestion was measuring against the wrong gateA gate in Tailwinds physically holds 50 departures a week — that's the hard limit the game enforces when you add a route, and it's the number the Airports tab has always shown you. The congestion warning on…
  • Jul 27A News tab — your world now has a memoryThe simulation has always generated far more story than you got to see. Rival airlines start fare wars, open second hubs, invest in cabins, run out of money and merge; the world economy moves through fuel…
  • Jul 26Contested routes now count your whole operationIf you flew a city pair with more than one aircraft, the Competition tab was only showing one of them. A route worked by an A220 at 47 flights a week and a turboprop at 18 reported a grand total of 18 — so a…
  • Jul 26Hub congestion now tracks flights, not routesGate congestion at your hubs used to count routes — so a twice-a-week regional spoke weighed exactly as much as a ten-a-day trunk route. That quietly punished the sensible move of building out domestic feed…
  • Jul 25Fleet tab: jump straight to a plane, service the whole fleet at onceTwo quality-of-life upgrades for anyone running a large fleet. Opening an aircraft is faster to get around, and keeping your planes airworthy no longer means clicking through them one at a time.
  • Jul 24Heavy maintenance: your fleet now visits the hangarAircraft don’t fly forever without care. Tailwinds now models the real airline maintenance calendar: your planes build up wear as they fly, and periodically they have to come out of service for a heavy check…
  • Jul 24Order big, pay less: bulk fleet discountsBuying aircraft now works the way it does in the real world, where nobody pays sticker price and a launch order of a hundred jets is a very different conversation from buying one. The more of a type you order…
  • Jul 24The home page is the front door againComing back to Tailwinds used to drop you straight onto your airline’s dashboard. Now every visit opens on the home page first — a calmer starting point before you dive back into the numbers.
  • Jul 23The aircraft picker now leads with your free planesA small tweak to the route-planning form that saves a lot of scrolling once your fleet grows.
  • Jul 22See your quality score everywhereQuality has always decided how passengers split between airlines — business travellers weigh it heavily — but until now you had to open each route to see yours. No longer.
  • Jul 21A polish pass across the whole gameA full sweep of the interface — every screen reviewed on desktop and phone, and twenty rough edges smoothed out in one go.
  • Jul 20Runways matter nowUntil today, any aircraft could serve any airport it could reach. No longer — every airport now has its longest runway on record, every aircraft has a minimum runway it needs, and the two have to agree before…
  • Jul 20A proper pass for phones and small screensPlayers told us the game felt cramped on a phone — the setup screen most of all. Here is a focused pass on small screens. Nothing about the desktop game changes.
  • Jul 20A table view for your gatesPlayer feedback strikes again: once an airline holds gates at thirty-plus airports, the Gates tab turned into a very long scroll. It now scales the same way the Routes page does.
  • Jul 19Codeshare partnerships are now unlimitedThe cap on bilateral codeshare agreements is gone — you can now partner with as many carriers as you like.
  • Jul 17Easier aircraft shopping and cabin planningA round of quality-of-life upgrades driven by player feedback, focused on the Market and the cabin configurator.
  • Jul 15Put idle hours to work: fly one plane on several routesAn aircraft with spare weekly flying hours can now open additional routes straight from the route planner — you no longer need a brand-new, fully idle plane for every route. If a jet or freighter is only…
  • Jul 15Route demand rebalanced against real-world trafficWe audited passenger demand on dozens of real city pairs against published airline traffic data — and the model needed work. The world's busiest real routes were tiny in the game, while some pairings that…
  • Jul 11Your airline, charted over timeThe Finance tab has a new Statistics page that turns your airline's history into charts — and lets you zoom from the last few weeks all the way out to decades.
  • Jul 11World events now actually ground passengersUntil now, a pandemic scare or recession quietly skimmed a percentage off your total revenue while every flight still showed a full cabin — confusing, and impossible to manage around. World events now shrink…
  • Jul 10Transfer routes between aircraftBy popular demand: you can now move an aircraft's entire schedule to another plane without tearing it down and rebuilding it. Open an aircraft on the Fleet page and hit Transfer Routes to pick a compatible…
  • Jul 10The great rebalance: running an airline is supposed to be hardMoney came too easily. Routes broke even at load factors no real airline could survive on, full planes at premium fares never attracted competition, and a profitable network became a money printer with no way…
  • Jul 10Loyalty rework: a long game with real money on the lineFrequent-flyer programs used to be a vending machine — fund one for a quarter, collect a permanent bonus. No longer. Loyalty is now a genuine long-term investment: expensive up front, compounding for years…
  • Jul 8Two new alliances: the value bloc and the emerging-market networkThe alliance map grows from three global blocs to five, giving more carriers — and more playstyles — a network to call home.
  • Jul 8The hub overhaul: focus cities, real connections, and fortress hubsThe biggest network update Tailwinds has shipped. Hubs are no longer a passive checkbox — they're a system you build, defend, and feel in every line of your P&L.
  • Jul 8Fixed: quality investments now count on multi-aircraft routes — and the Alliances page stops lyingPlayers reported being unable to push their quality score past ~60 — thanks for flagging it, and for the follow-up reports. It turned out to be TWO bugs:
  • Jul 7Unions arrive: strikes and contract negotiationsUnderpaying your people is no longer a slow, quiet drag on quality — labor relations now have teeth.
  • Jul 7Quality overhaul: earned reputations and cabins that matterThe quality system got a deep rework — your product choices now do exactly what they say, and your customer rating is something you earn.
  • Jul 7On-time performance: it takes a whole airline (and a rested fleet)Your on-time rate used to depend on pilot morale alone. Now it reflects how airlines actually run:
  • Jul 7Freighters now look like freightersSeveral cargo aircraft in the market — the 757-200PF, MD-11F, DC-10-30F, 727-200F, A321P2F, and 767-200SF — were showing photos of their passenger cousins. They now show proper freighter photos, windowless…
  • Jul 7Add Flights fixed, and no more silent dead endsA player on Discord reported that "Add Flights" sometimes did nothing — thanks for the report! The button could look ready while the game quietly refused the request. All of those dead ends are fixed:
  • Jul 6Smarter passengers, real marketing, and big-network toolsThis update makes demand feel much more alive, and gives players with large networks the management tools they've been asking for.
  • Jul 5Competitors that actually competeThe biggest AI update since launch. Rival airlines are no longer static route lists — they run their businesses:
  • Jul 4Bulk pricing toolsReprice routes in bulk: filter by occupancy (find everything under 60% load in one click), select route cards, and adjust fares together instead of one dialog at a time.
  • Jun 24Double deckers arriveThe A380 and 747 family are now in the marketplace, with a Double Decker filter to find them. Can your network actually fill 500 seats? The flagship guide will help you decide.
  • Jun 21Branding & freight polishIn-game branding editor: upload your own logo, or use the built-in system — neutral greyscale bases with your accent colour driving the motif. Rename and recolour your airline any time.
  • Jun 19Tailwinds goes mobileInstall it like an app. Tailwinds is now a progressive web app: add it to your home screen for a full-screen experience, with offline start once cached.

Older changes predate this devlog. From June 2026 on, every significant update gets an entry.
